mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened financing conditions that reduce corporate investment and consumer spending.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return does not deviate from the pre-rates rise average by more than one standard deviation, or the 5-day realized volatility of SPX is not elevated during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) of at least 5,000 suggests weakening labor market strength, which is associated with negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as investors anticipate slower earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous_month + 5000 and consecutive month increase
failure_condition: During periods meeting the trigger, the 60-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior month's return (t-test p > 0.10), or the SPX 6-month realized volatility is not elevated.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 2 percentage points, it signals robust economic momentum that drives a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as market anticipates continued demand for equities.
failure_condition: Across 10 such triggers, the 20-day forward returns do not exceed the mean by more than one standard deviation, or the SPX 20-day autocorrelation is not significantly higher than zero.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of at least 0.3% indicates an early inflationary pressure, which, when combined with rising labor costs (HOUST), produces a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as investors anticipate rate hikes.
failure_condition: During 5 such inflationary triggers, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (one-tailed t-test p > 0.05), or the SPX 5-day realized volatility is not elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals a strong labor market, which, when coupled with falling inflation (CPIAUCSL), creates a 'soft landing' narrative that drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 250 (index units)
regime_hint: Labor market strength with cooling inflation
failure_condition: Over 10 such regimes, the 20-day forward returns do not beat the neutral benchmark (zero return) with a Sharpe ratio > 0.5, or the SPX 20-day autocorrelation is not significantly positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-time spike in retail employment (PAYEMS) of at least 20,000 above the prior month's level, without a corresponding rise in industrial production, predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return due to market uncertainty about job market quality.
failure_condition: During 5 such spikes, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (one-tailed p > 0.10), or the SPX 5-day realized skewness is not significantly negative.

mechanism_narrative: A 2 consecutive months of declining retail sales (implied proxy via HOUST) combined with a sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals weak demand and supply-side constraints.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous_month AND HOUST < previous_to_previous_month AND INDPRO < previous_month AND INDPRO < previous_to_previous_month
failure_condition: Over 8 such contraction episodes, the 60-day forward returns do not underperform the 60-day risk-free rate by at least one basis point, or the SPX 60-day realized skewness is not significantly negative.

mechanism_narrative: A long-term upward trend in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for 12 consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as market anticipates higher future earnings and rate hike risk.
failure_condition: Across 24 months of such inflation trends, the 20-day forward returns do not outperform the 20-day risk-free rate by more than one standard deviation, or the SPX 20-day autocorrelation is not significantly positive.
